'''Ahmet Nihat Berker''' (born 20 September 1949) is a [[Turkish people|Turkish]] scientist, [[theoretical chemist]], [[physicist]] and [[emeritus professor]] of [[physics]] at [[MIT]]. Currently, he is the acting [[Dean (education)|dean]] of Engineering and Natural Sciences in [[Kadir Has University]], Turkey. He is the son of a notable scientist and engineer, [[:tr:Ratip Berker|Ratip Berker]]. His wife, Bedia Erim Berker,<ref>[http://web.mit.edu/physics/berker/album.html Bedia Erim Berker], [[Technical University of Istanbul]],</ref> is a professor of [[chemistry]] at [[Istanbul Technical University]], and one of his sons, Selim Berker, is a professor of [[epistemology]] in the department of [[philosophy]] at [[Harvard University]].<ref>[http://philosophy.fas.harvard.edu/people/selim-berker Selim Berker], [http://philosophy.fas.harvard.edu/people/research-interests/ethics ethics] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151124113628/http://philosophy.fas.harvard.edu/people/research-interests/ethics |date=24 November 2015 }} and [http://philosophy.fas.harvard.edu/people/research-interests/epistemology epistemology] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151124113352/http://philosophy.fas.harvard.edu/people/research-interests/epistemology |date=24 November 2015 }} professor.</ref><ref>[http://scholar.harvard.edu/files/sberker/files/berker-cv-oct20-2015_0.pdf?m=1445366026 Selim Berker] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119232624/http://scholar.harvard.edu/files/sberker/files/berker-cv-oct20-2015_0.pdf?m=1445366026 |date=19 November 2015}}, [http://scholar.harvard.edu/sberker Department of Philosophy], [[Harvard University]].</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://web.mit.edu/physics/berker/index.html | title=Prof. A. Nihat Berker, Kadir Has University &#124; Professor of Physics, Emeritus}}</ref>

==Academic life==
After graduating from [[Robert College]] at first place in 1967, Berker received B.S. degrees in physics and chemistry from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in 1971. He received his M.S. and PhD degrees in physics from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] in 1972 and 1977, respectively. During 1977–79, he was a postdoctoral research fellow in the department of physics at Harvard University.<ref name="vita">[http://web.mit.edu/physics/berker/docs/ANBerkerCV2017.pdf?201704227 Prof. A. Nihat Berker]</ref> He was an assistant professor during 1979–82, associate professor during 1982–1988, and professor of [[theoretical physics]] during 1988–04 at MIT. From 1999 to 2004, he served as a professor and dean of the School of Sciences and Letters at the [[Istanbul Technical University]]. After losing the [[Rector (academia)|president ''(rector)'']] elections in [[İTÜ]],<ref>{{cite web|title=İTÜ elections|date=July 2004 |url=http://www.itusozluk.com/goster.php/it%FC+rekt%F6rl%FCk+se%E7imi+sonu%E7lar%FD}}</ref> he left the [[Technical University of Istanbul]] for a professor position at [[Koç University]]. He became emeritus professor of physics at MIT in 2004. He was an adjunct professor at [[Boğaziçi University]] in [[Bebek, Istanbul]], between 1996 and 2004, as well. During 2005–2009, he served as a professor of physics at Koç University in Istanbul. From 2009 until his resignation on 11 September 2016,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sozcu.com.tr/2016/egitim/sabanci-universitesi-rektoru-nihat-berker-istifa-etti-1441293/ | trans-title=Nihat Berker resigns as the president of Sabancı University | title=Sabancı Üniversitesi Rektörü Nihat Berker istifa etti | publisher=Sözcü Gazetesi | language=tr | date=11 September 2016 | access-date=27 January 2019 }}</ref> he was the president of [[Sabancı University]] in [[Tuzla]], Istanbul. Currently, he is the acting dean of the faculty of engineering and natural sciences at [[Kadir Has University]].<ref name="vita" />

===Research areas===
Nihat Berker is best known for his research in [[statistical mechanics]], especially on [[phase transition]]s applying [[renormalization group]] theory, with applications to [[surface physics]] and materials with [[geometric frustration|defect]]s.
